slices.responsibility: Catalog owner changes only its recorded source responsibility to return the stored inventoryRevision for known SKUs while preserving existing availability and unknown-SKU behavior. Orders owner changes only its recorded source responsibility to emit the exact v2 envelope, copying occurredAt, locale, and the Catalog-provided inventoryRevision and nesting id, sku, and quantity under order with no retained v1 flat fields. Deploy Catalog before enabling Orders v2 publication. Run npm test in both repositories and record accepted commits, tests, and unresolved issues in each repository handoff.

Prepare the event consumer before Orders publishes v2. Branch validation by version: retain the current v1 flat contract and accept the required v2 nested contract; reject other types, unsupported versions, missing or wrongly typed required fields, invalid nested orders, and non-positive/non-integer quantities without changing deliveries. Normalize the order ID per version and deduplicate accepted deliveries solely by event.id, including repeated v1 or v2 delivery. Run npm test and record the accepted commit, compatibility coverage, tests, and unresolved issues in the repository handoff.

Preserve orderId and status exactly and add eventVersion from event.version, without coupling the response adapter to v2-only order layout so rolling v1 responses remain representable. Roll out after v2 publication is safe, then run npm test and record the accepted commit, tests, and unresolved issues in the repository handoff. After all slices converge, run the Coordinator public integration test without making Coordinator part of a writable slice.

risks: The visible Notifications test covers v2 idempotency but not retained v1, unsupported versions, malformed fields, or cross-delivery event-ID behavior; those cases remain mandatory acceptance coverage.

Adding eventVersion is API-additive, but downstream Gateway clients that reject unknown response fields could still be incompatible despite orderId and status remaining stable.

All five baseline public test runs currently fail as expected: Catalog omits inventoryRevision, Orders still emits v1, Notifications rejects v2, Gateway omits eventVersion, and Coordinator observes v1. No implementation was performed in this design-only turn.

Within rollout, make the additive Catalog field available before enabling Orders v2 publication, and publish only after both consumer slices are prepared.

Prepare the event consumer first: explicitly validate and accept the retained flat v1 shape and the nested v2 shape, reject unsupported versions/types and malformed required fields without mutating deliveries, normalize the order ID per version, and preserve event-ID idempotency. Add tests for valid v1, valid v2, duplicate IDs, unsupported versions, malformed envelopes, and unchanged delivery state after rejection.

Prepare the response adapter before v2 publication by preserving orderId and status exactly and adding eventVersion from event.version. Test stable fields and version exposure; the additive field allows the adapter to report either v1 or v2 during rollout.

risks: The current Notifications test covers only valid v2 and duplicate delivery; retained v1, malformed-event rejection, unsupported-version rejection, and rejection-without-state-mutation remain untested.
The current in-memory/injected Map models idempotency only within the supplied delivery store; persistence and cross-process atomicity are outside the recorded repository boundary.
Orders must not publish v2 before Notifications is dual-reading, or valid v2 events will be rejected during the rolling deployment.
Catalog and Orders share one implementation slice but have a runtime ordering constraint: Orders v2 publication depends on Catalog already returning inventoryRevision.
Baseline tests all fail as expected: gateway lacks eventVersion, catalog omits inventoryRevision, orders still emits v1, notifications rejects v2, and coordinator observes v1 instead of v2.
